The first Homo sapiensis evidence from Indochina is from a site in northeast Laos dated to 70 ± 10 ka.

the Tam Pa Ling snail record indicates a major climatic change at 70 ka, with a shift towards more open environments in the LGM, and the return to forested environments in the early Holocene.

the environmental conditions at Tam Pà Linh, Laos, were favorable for modern human occupation during the Late Pleistocene.

the LGM was a key event for the environmental history of the region, with a strong impact on the local vegetation, and thus on the availability of resources for the first modern humans.
